page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is relatively low, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories respectively. However, the instance leverages its 16 physical cores to deliver average multi-core performance, as demonstrated by average ratings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached and uncached reads and writes also perform in the average tier, though the Passmark memory score is weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

With its high memory density and average multi-threaded capabilities, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. Factual benchmark results show average performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving. It also handles smaller LLM inference tasks at average speeds, though performance drops to weak for medium-sized models. Given the lack of local storage and modest network bandwidth, it is best utilized for memory-cached databases, medium-scale web serving, and software compilation tasks where memory capacity is the primary constraint.
